- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 1455-1460, _heal_intake_scope_guard_permits_create after the LAST RUN body_missing addition
  Problem: The LAST RUN added a body_missing branch but jq input-generation failure and verify-tool failure both still fall through to the same `unavailable` status. After the LAST RUN, an operator who sees `reason=scope_marker_unverified status=unavailable` still cannot tell whether `jq` failed to write the input JSON or whether `heal-scope verify` returned a non-`verified` status (or was missing). The new branch distinguishes only "body missing" from "everything else".
  Why it fails at runtime: When jq is missing or its stdin redirect fails (the `> "${scope_guard_input}" 2>/dev/null` after the elif), the elif's command list does not execute, `scope_guard_status` stays empty, and the later `printf … | tr -cd … | head -c 40` plus `[ -n … ] || … = "unavailable"` collapse the case to `unavailable`. The CRITICAL alert then says only "scope marker could not be verified (unavailable)", leaving the on-call to guess between jq-unavailable, verify-unavailable, and verify-malformed.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 1445-1451, the disabled-path `exit 0`
  Problem: The `exit 0` in the disabled branch is in `_heal_intake_scope_guard_permits_create`, but it terminates the whole intake script. Any caller-level state-file write or post-cleanup that a future maintainer adds immediately after `_open_issue` returns would be silently skipped when the guard is off (it would also be skipped in the verified/refused paths because the function either returns or fires `exit 0`/`return 1` from the same call site).
  Why it fails at runtime: Today the call site has no post-action, so the path is latent, but it bakes in a foot-gun for the next maintainer.
  SEVERITY: NIT

- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: From the linked issue, the README table cell, the agents.d fragment, and the changelog fragment all converge on the same documented behavior for the default-off path: the intake "composes the heal issue, logs `WORKFLOW_HEAL skip reason=scope_guard_disabled` and … files nothing (no issue, label or outcome comment)". README adds: "exits 0 without creating the issue, its labels or the outcome comment, so no heal issues are filed until an operator sets it."
  Expected change site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh at lines 913-914, immediately before the `case "${ACTION}" in` decision (the `ensure_label_exists "${HEAL_LABEL}" "${SELF_REPO}" || true` and `ensure_label_exists "${ESCALATED_LABEL}" "${SELF_REPO}" || true` calls).
  Evidence of absence: Lines 913-914 unconditionally create `ai:workflow-heal` and `ai:workflow-heal-escalated` on SELF_REPO for every classification (`duplicate`, `escalate`, `budget_exhausted`, `open`) before the budget-action case statement runs and before the scope guard inside `_open_issue` is ever consulted. With `HEAL_INTAKE_SCOPE_GUARD_ENABLED=false` (the default the PR ships), the scope guard at line 1450 calls `exit 0` and `_open_issue` never reaches `gh issue create`, so the labels created at 913-914 have no consumer. This contradicts the documented "no … label … comment" guarantee. The LAST RUN DIFF did not move or gate these calls, and the agents.d / README / changelog fragments added by the PR are unchanged in the LAST RUN. The intent (no labels when off) and the implementation (labels created unconditionally before the guard) diverge on these two lines.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
